passages.text: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of hundreds and of thousands.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had people with him.
David counted the people who were with him.
David appointed leaders over the people.
David chose commanders over groups of a thousand.
David chose commanders over groups of a hundred.
passages.original: וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י מֵאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had people with him.
David divided his troops into three groups.
He put Joab in charge of one third of the troops.
He put Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and Joab’s brother, in charge of another third.
He put Ittai the Gittite in charge of the last third.
David spoke to his people.
David said, “I will go out with you also.”
passages.original: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח דָּוִ֜ד אֶת־ הָעָ֗ם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית בְּיַד־ יוֹאָב֙ וְ֠הַשְּׁלִשִׁית בְּיַ֨ד אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָה֙ אֲחִ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב וְהַ֨שְּׁלִשִׁ֔ת בְּיַ֖ד אִתַּ֣י הַגִּתִּ֑יס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם יָצֹ֥א אֵצֵ֛א גַּם־ אֲנִ֖י עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will pay no attention to us. Even if half of us die, they will not care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better for now if you support us from the city.”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to King David.
They said, “You must not go out with us.”
They explained, “If we run away, the enemy will not care about us.”
They said, “If half of us die, the enemy will not care about us.”
They told David, “You are worth more than ten thousand of us.”
They said, “It is better if you stay in the city.”
They asked David to help them from the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הָעָ֜ם לֹ֣א תֵצֵ֗א כִּי֩ אִם־ נֹ֨ס נָנ֜וּס לֹא־ יָשִׂ֧ימוּ אֵלֵ֣ינוּ לֵ֗ב וְאִם־ יָמֻ֤תוּ חֶצְיֵ֙נוּ֙ לֹֽא־ יָשִׂ֤ימוּ אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ לֵ֔ב כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֥ה כָמֹ֖נוּ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה אֲלָפִ֑ים וְעַתָּ֣ה ט֔וֹב כִּי־ תִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֥נוּ מֵעִ֖יר לַעְזִיר׃ס

passages.text: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
passages.sermon:
David was the king.
The people asked David not to go out to battle with them.
David answered the people.
He said, “I will do whatever seems best to you.”
David stood beside the gate.
All the troops marched out from the city.
They went out in groups of hundreds and thousands.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ יִיטַ֥ב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם אֶעֱשֶׂ֑ה וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ יַ֣ד הַשַּׁ֔עַר וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ יָֽצְא֔וּ לְמֵא֖וֹת וְלַאֲלָפִֽים׃

passages.text: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to his commanders.
He spoke to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai.
He gave them a command.
He said, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.”
All the people heard the king’s command.
They heard the king order all the commanders about Absalom.
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־ י֠וֹאָב וְאֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־ אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְאַט־ לִ֖י לַנַּ֣עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּצַוֺּ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים עַל־ דְּבַ֥ר אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel in the battle, which took place in the forest of Ephraim.
passages.sermon:
David was the king.
David had an army.
David’s army marched into the field.
They went to fight against the army of Israel.
The battle happened in the forest of Ephraim.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֛ם הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לִקְרַ֣את יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בְּיַ֥עַר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had loyal servants who fought for him.
The people of Israel fought against David’s servants.
David’s servants defeated the people of Israel in battle.
A great slaughter happened that day.
Twenty thousand men died.
passages.original: וַיִּנָּ֤גְפוּ שָׁם֙ עַ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֞ם הַמַּגֵּפָ֧ה גְדוֹלָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃

passages.text: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
passages.sermon:
The battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
The fighting spread across the whole land.
Many people died that day.
The forest killed more people than the sword did.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי־ שָׁ֧ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה נָפֹצֵית עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיֶּ֤רֶב הַיַּ֙עַר֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל בָּעָ֔ם מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָכְלָ֛ה הַחֶ֖רֶב בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom rode on a mule.
He met the servants of David.
The mule carried Absalom under the thick branches of a large oak tree.
Absalom’s head became caught in the tree.
The mule kept going and left Absalom behind.
Absalom hung between heaven and earth.
He was suspended in midair.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּרֵא֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְאַבְשָׁל֞וֹם רֹכֵ֣ב עַל־ הַפֶּ֗רֶד וַיָּבֹ֣א הַפֶּ֡רֶד תַּ֣חַת שׂוֹבֶךְ֩ הָאֵלָ֨ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֜ה וַיֶּחֱזַ֧ק רֹאשׁ֣וֹ בָאֵלָ֗ה וַיֻּתַּן֙ בֵּ֤ין הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהַפֶּ֥רֶד אֲשֶׁר־ תַּחְתָּ֖יו עָבָֽר׃

passages.text: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
passages.sermon:
A man saw something happen.
He saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.
The man went to Joab.
He spoke to Joab.
He said, “I saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree.”
passages.original: וַיַּרְא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם תָּל֖וּי בָּאֵלָֽה׃

passages.text: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab spoke to the man who brought him news.
Joab said, “You saw Absalom.”
Joab asked, “Why did you not strike Absalom down on the spot?”
Joab said, “I would have given you ten pieces of silver.”
Joab said, “I would have given you a warrior’s belt.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב לָאִישׁ֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ וְהִנֵּ֣ה רָאִ֔יתָ וּמַדּ֛וּעַ לֹֽא־ הִכִּית֥וֹ שָׁ֖ם אָ֑רְצָה וְעָלַ֗י לָ֤תֶת לְךָ֙ עֲשָׂ֣רָה כֶ֔סֶף וַחֲגֹרָ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃

passages.text: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Joab.
He said, “I will not harm the king’s son.
You could give me a thousand pieces of silver.
I still would not raise my hand against him.
The king gave a command.
We all heard it.
He told you, Abishai, and Ittai.
He said, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וְלֹא אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁקֵ֤ל עַל־ כַּפַּי֙ אֶ֣לֶף כֶּ֔סֶף לֹֽא־ אֶשְׁלַ֥ח יָדִ֖י אֶל־ בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י בְאָזְנֵ֜ינוּ צִוָּ֣ה הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֹ֠תְךָ וְאֶת־ אֲבִישַׁ֤י וְאֶת־ אִתַּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שִׁמְרוּ־ מִ֕י בַּנַּ֖עַר בְּאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: If I had jeopardized my own life —and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”
passages.sermon:
The man spoke to Joab.
He said, “If I had risked my own life,
The king would know everything.
Nothing is hidden from the king.
You would not protect me.
You would stand apart from me.”
passages.original: אֽוֹ־ עָשִׂ֤יתִי בְנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁ֔קֶר וְכָל־ דָּבָ֖ר לֹא־ יִכָּחֵ֣ד מִן־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב מִנֶּֽגֶד׃

passages.text: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of King David’s army.
Joab spoke to the man.
Joab said, “I will not wait like this with you.”
Joab took three spears in his hand.
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom was still alive.
Absalom was caught in the branches of a large oak tree.
Joab thrust the three spears into Absalom’s heart.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֔ב לֹא־ כֵ֖ן אֹחִ֣ילָה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיִּקַּח֩ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה שְׁבָטִ֜ים בְּכַפּ֗וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֵם֙ בְּלֵ֣ב אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם עוֹדֶ֥נּוּ חַ֖י בְּלֵ֥ב הָאֵלָֽה׃

passages.text: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
passages.sermon:
Ten young men served Joab.
These young men carried Joab’s armor.
They surrounded Absalom.
They struck Absalom.
They killed Absalom.
passages.original: וַיָּסֹ֙בּוּ֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֣י יוֹאָ֑ב וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם וַיְמִיתֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab blew the ram’s horn.
The troops heard the sound.
The troops stopped chasing Israel.
Joab had ordered the troops to stop.
Joab restrained the people.
passages.original: וַיִּתְקַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ בַּשֹּׁפָ֔ר וַיָּ֣שָׁב הָעָ֔ם מִרְדֹ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי־ חָשַׂ֥ךְ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Joab’s men killed Absalom in the forest.
They took Absalom’s body.
They threw his body into a large pit in the forest.
They piled a very large heap of stones over his body.
All the Israelites saw what happened.
Each Israelite ran away.
Each man returned to his own home.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם וַיַּשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אֹת֤וֹ בַיַּ֙עַר֙ אֶל־ הַפַּ֣חַת הַגָּד֔וֹל וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ עָלָ֛יו גַּל־ אֲבָנִ֖ים גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֑ד וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְאָהֳלוֹ׃ס

passages.text: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom lived during the time of King David in Israel.
Absalom set up a pillar for himself.
He did this while he was still alive.
He placed the pillar in the King’s Valley.
Absalom said, “I have no son to keep my name alive.”
He wanted his name to be remembered.
Absalom named the pillar after himself.
People call it Absalom’s Monument.
They still use this name today.
passages.original: וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֣ם לָקַ֗ח וַיַּצֶּב־ ל֤וֹ בְחַיָּו אֶת־ מַצֶּ֙בֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעֵֽמֶק־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֤י אָמַר֙ אֵֽין־ לִ֣י בֵ֔ן בַּעֲב֖וּר הַזְכִּ֣יר שְׁמִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לַמַּצֶּ֙בֶת֙ עַל־ שְׁמ֔וֹ וַיִּקָּ֤רֵא לָהּ֙ יַ֣ד אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.
Ahimaaz spoke.
He said, “Let me run to the king.
I want to bring news to the king.
The LORD has judged the king’s enemies.
The LORD has rescued the king from his enemies.”
passages.original: וַאֲחִימַ֤עַץ בֶּן־ צָדוֹק֙ אָמַ֔ר אָר֣וּצָה נָּ֔א וַאֲבַשְּׂרָ֖ה אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּי־ שְׁפָט֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה מִיַּ֥ד אֹיְבָֽיו׃

passages.text: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of King David’s army.
Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.
Joab spoke to Ahimaaz.
Joab said, “You are not the right person to bring news today.”
Joab said, “You may bring news on another day.”
Joab said, “You must not bring news today.”
Joab said, “The king’s son has died.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יוֹאָ֗ב לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ בְּשֹׂרָ֤ה אַתָּה֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וּבִשַּׂרְתָּ֖ בְּי֣וֹם אַחֵ֑ר וְהַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לֹ֣א תְבַשֵּׂ֔ר כִּֽי־ עַל בֶּן־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֵֽת׃

passages.text: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of the army.
A Cushite was present with Joab.
Joab spoke to the Cushite.
Joab said, “Go to the king.”
Joab said, “Tell the king what you have seen.”
The Cushite bowed to Joab.
The Cushite ran to the king.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹאָב֙ לַכּוּשִׁ֔י לֵ֛ךְ הַגֵּ֥ד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֑יתָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ כוּשִׁ֛י לְיוֹאָ֖ב וַיָּרֹֽץ׃

passages.text: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “Regardless of whatever may happen, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.
Ahimaaz spoke to Joab.
Ahimaaz insisted.
He said, “No matter what happens, let me run after the Cushite.”
Joab answered him.
Joab said, “My son, why do you want to run?”
Joab said, “You will not receive a reward.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֜וֹד אֲחִימַ֤עַץ בֶּן־ צָדוֹק֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב וִ֣יהִי מָ֔ה אָרֻֽצָה־ נָּ֥א גַם־ אָ֖נִי אַחֲרֵ֣י הַכּוּשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֗ב לָֽמָּה־ זֶּ֞ה אַתָּ֥ה רָץ֙ בְּנִ֔י וּלְכָ֖ה אֵין־ בְּשׂוֹרָ֥ה מֹצֵֽאת׃

passages.text: “No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.
Ahimaaz wanted to run after the Cushite.
Joab was the commander.
Ahimaaz said, “No matter what, I want to run!”
Joab said to him, “Run!”
Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain.
Ahimaaz outran the Cushite.
passages.original: וִיהִי־ מָ֣ה אָר֔וּץ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ ר֑וּץ וַיָּ֤רָץ אֲחִימַ֙עַץ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַכִּכָּ֔ר וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־ הַכּוּשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David sat between two gates.
A watchman was present.
The watchman went up to the roof of the gateway.
The gateway was by the wall.
The watchman lifted his eyes.
The watchman looked out.
The watchman saw a man.
The man was running.
The man was running alone.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֥ד יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בֵּין־ שְׁנֵ֣י הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַצֹּפֶ֜ה אֶל־ גַּ֤ג הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ אֶל־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וַיִּשָּׂ֤א אֶת־ עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה־ אִ֖ישׁ רָ֥ץ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.” As the first runner drew near, the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.
passages.sermon:
The watchman stood on the wall.
He saw a man running alone.
The watchman called out.
He told the king what he saw.
The king answered him.
The king said, “If he is alone, he brings good news.”
The first runner came closer.
The watchman looked again.
He saw another man running alone.
The watchman called to the gatekeeper.
He said, “Look, another man is running alone.”
The king spoke again.
The king said, “This one also brings good news.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א הַצֹּפֶה֙ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ לְבַדּ֖וֹ בְּשׂוֹרָ֣ה בְּפִ֑יו וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וְקָרֵֽב׃ וַיַּ֣רְא הַצֹּפֶה֮ אִישׁ־ אַחֵ֣ר רָץ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א הַצֹּפֶה֙ אֶל־ הַשֹּׁעֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־ אִ֖ישׁ רָ֣ץ לְבַדּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ גַּם־ זֶ֥ה מְבַשֵּֽׂר׃

passages.text: The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
passages.sermon:
The watchman looked at the first man running.
The watchman said, "He runs like Ahimaaz."
Ahimaaz is the son of Zadok.
The king heard the watchman.
The king said, "This man is good."
The king said, "He brings good news."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַצֹּפֶ֔ה אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ אֶת־ מְרוּצַ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן כִּמְרֻצַ֖ת אֲחִימַ֣עַץ בֶּן־ צָד֑וֹק וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אִֽישׁ־ ט֣וֹב זֶ֔ה וְאֶל־ בְּשׂוֹרָ֥ה טוֹבָ֖ה יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz was a faithful messenger.
He called out to King David.
He said, “All is well!”
Ahimaaz bowed down before the king.
He put his face to the ground.
He said, “Blessed be the LORD your God!”
The LORD has handed over the men.
These men lifted their hands against you, my lord the king.
God has given you victory over them.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֲחִימַ֗עַץ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שָׁל֔וֹם וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לְאַפָּ֖יו אָ֑רְצָהס וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּרוּךְ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר סִגַּר֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ נָשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־ יָדָ֖ם בַּֽאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
Absalom was his son.
Ahimaaz was the son of Zadok.
Ahimaaz was a messenger.
Joab was the commander of David’s army.

The king spoke to Ahimaaz.
The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom safe?”
Ahimaaz answered the king.
Ahimaaz said, “I saw a great crowd.”
Joab sent the king’s servant and me.”
“I do not know what happened.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁל֥וֹם לַנַּ֖עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחִימַ֡עַץ רָאִיתִי֩ הֶהָמ֨וֹן הַגָּד֜וֹל לִ֠שְׁלֹחַ אֶת־ עֶ֨בֶד הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ יוֹאָב֙ וְאֶת־ עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי מָֽה׃

passages.text: “Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke.
He said, "Move aside."
He said, "Stand here."
Ahimaaz moved aside.
Ahimaaz stood in that place.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ סֹ֖ב הִתְיַצֵּ֣ב כֹּ֑ה וַיִּסֹּ֖ב וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽד׃

passages.text: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
passages.sermon:
The Cushite arrived.
The Cushite spoke to the king.
The Cushite said, “My lord the king, I bring good news.”
The LORD has judged in your favor today.
The LORD has delivered you.
He has saved you from all who rose up against you.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכּוּשִׁ֖י בָּ֑א וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַכּוּשִׁ֗י יִתְבַּשֵּׂר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ שְׁפָטְךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם מִיַּ֖ד כָּל־ הַקָּמִ֥ים עָלֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May what has become of the young man happen to the enemies of my lord the king and to all who rise up against you to harm you.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to the Cushite messenger.
David was the king of Israel.
Absalom was David’s son.
David asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom safe?”
The Cushite answered David.
The Cushite said, “May your enemies be like that young man.”
The Cushite meant Absalom’s fate should come to all who oppose you.
The Cushite said, “May all who rise up against you to harm you be like him.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ הַכּוּשִׁ֔י הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לַנַּ֖עַר לְאַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַכּוּשִׁ֗י יִהְי֤וּ כַנַּ֙עַר֙ אֹֽיְבֵי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ קָ֥מוּ עָלֶ֖יךָ לְרָעָֽה׃ס

passages.text: The king was shaken and went up to the gate chamber and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
passages.sermon:
King David heard that his son Absalom was dead.
David felt deep sorrow.
David was shaken.
David went up to the room above the city gate.
David wept there.
As David walked, he cried out.
David said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!”
David wished he could have died instead of Absalom.
David said, “If only I had died in your place, Absalom, my son, my son!”
passages.original: וַיִּרְגַּ֣ז הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּ֛עַל עַל־ עֲלִיַּ֥ת הַשַּׁ֖עַר וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וְכֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר בְּלֶכְתּ֗וֹ בְּנִ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ בְּנִ֣י בְנִ֣י אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֤ן מוּתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י תַחְתֶּ֔יךָ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי׃
